text:
alex: Incident bot: paging — multiple model load failures in us-west-2 causing elevated 5xxs on /v1/generate :rotating_light:
oncall-bot: @ops-rotation you are on call for incidents (see runbook). Auto-triage: OOM-at-load + deserialization errors + compile-timeouts on newer kernel images.
priya: Confirming — hitting OOM during model init on gpu-23/gpu-24. Container restarts looped. Crash log snippet below:
```
KeyError during decode: unexpected EOF while reading weights
cudaDriverFatal: device-side assert triggered (code 4)
RuntimeError: allocations failed: requested 11.2G, available 8.0G
```
infra-sre: Node-level metrics show memory pressure + swap spikes (paging) right before OOM. Looks like shard demux/kv-cache growth triggered during deserial.
julia: Customer impact: two enterprise routes (cust-42, cust-77) saw degraded responses between 14:03-14:07 PST; approx 3.4% of hosted traffic got 5xx or timeouts, escalation email sent.
alex: Mitigation plan (live):
- Step 1: Evict noncritical low-priority models on the affected nodes to free GPU RAM. (manual until autoscaler policy updated)
- Step 2: Disable JIT compile for the failing model variant so we skip long compile timeouts and fall back to interpreter path.
- Step 3: Pin requests for the enterprise routes to fallback quantized variant (fp16/4bit) in the routing layer.
priya: I'm evicting models now on gpu-23. Command: ```kubectl -n inference exec -it loaderctl -- ./evict_model --node gpu-23 --keep=critical```
infra-sre: Eviction done on gpu-23/gpu-24, freed ~9.4G each. Node swap dropped. Starting warmup of fp16 shard on gpu-23.
oncall-bot: Handoff: @ops-rotation please take over for 15m while I update incident channel and runbook.
ops-rotation: Taking it. Quick status: compile disabled, warmup for fallback shard running, watching for container restarts.
julia: Noted on customer comms — sending a short status update to affected customers with ETA ~20m for stable routing.
priya: Observed one deserialization error tied to an older artifact checksum mismatch; artifact fetch retried twice then moved to local fallback. Logs: ```artifact fetch failed checksum mismatch 0x9f3a -> using local cached copy```
alex: Temporary config patch applied to model-loader to increase init timeout from 90s -> 240s to accommodate slower deserial on overloaded nodes. Patch diff: ```-init_timeout: 90s
+init_timeout: 240s```
infra-sre: Note — increasing timeout trades latency for stability; will revert after full mitigation. Also adding a hotfix to avoid parallel KV cache prefill when swap > 1GB.
ops-rotation: After changes, container restarts dropped to zero for ~10m. 5xx rate for affected routes down to baseline.
julia: Customer-ops confirmed clients for cust-42 and cust-77 accepted the update. No data loss. Logging shows a small quality delta for the quantized fallback; ops-slo remains met.
alex: Post-incident next actions (to sync later):
- Reconcile faulty artifact leading to deserialization checksum mismatch and retire bad build.
- Add autoscaler rule to preferentially evict noncritical shards when swap > 800MB.
- Add model-loader feature flag to disable parallel compile on high memory pressure.
- Run replayed load test (staging) with new kernel image and JIT disabled to reproduce compile-timeouts.
priya: Creating follow-up issue with stack traces + node dumps. Will attach gcore and container logs.
```
Commands collected:
- gcore /proc/<pid> (on crash)
- kubectl -n inference logs <pod> --previous
- runc state <container> (to check oom info)
```
infra-sre: Scheduling a small deploy window to roll back the kernel image that correlated with increase in deserial failures. Tentative: 2AM UTC.
oncall-bot: Incident severity updated -> SEV2 (customer-visible but contained).
alex: Thx all. ops-rotation keep monitoring for 30m and escalate to eng-runtime if restarts return.
ops-rotation: Will do. Leaving channel but will update headcount if anything flips. :thumbsup:
customer-ops: Sent final update to customers at 14:28 PST with mitigation summary and timeline for root-cause follow-up.
julia: Closing incident thread when postmortem doc created.
